deepDiveThesesUsed.summary: Apps advertise '60+ supported models' but the vendored llama.cpp build only recognizes specific LLM_ARCH_* tags, so many trending releases (e.g. Qwen3.x) silently can't load.

The GGUF quant label (e.g. Q4_K_M) is not a standardized artifact — different quantizers (and even a vendor's own official QAT release) produce measurably different quality/size under the identical nominal tag.

The app's July 10 Swift rewrite fixed the July 7 staleness gap by fetching llama.cpp's latest GitHub release at build time instead of a pinned old commit, but that fetch resolves 'latest' fresh every build with no pinned tag and no version ever surfaced to the user, so two builds cut hours or days apart can silently embed different sets of supported architectures with no way to tell which one shipped. Backed by real llama.cpp release-cadence data (3 tags in under 3 hours) and PR merge-time data (~1 day to 24 days depending on whether an architecture is genuinely new). Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-07 thesis: static staleness vs. dynamic non-determinism.

A byte-identical GGUF file (LFM2.5-350M, 355 MB) loaded through the identical inference engine costs 56-85 MB of RAM on Apple Silicon/visionOS devices and 300-330 MB on Android/Linux SBC devices (Cactus Compute's own cross-platform benchmark, 2026-03-31) — a ~6x spread from the same bytes, caused by mmap()'d pages staying reclaimable file-backed memory on Apple platforms but frequently degrading to anonymous (fully-resident) memory on Android due to SELinux/vendor memory management. Breaks the industry-standard 'minRamMb = fileSize x constant' sizing heuristic (including privateSLM's own) since RAM cost is shown to be an OS/paging property, not a fixed property of the file. Distinct from the three prior theses: none of those were about post-load runtime memory footprint — 07-07 was about architecture recognition, 07-09 about quant-label inconsistency across quantizers, 07-13 about which engine version a build embeds. This one is about what happens to RAM once a model both is recognized AND has loaded.

What changed since 2026-07-09: privateslm's main branch pivoted from Flutter to a native SwiftUI + llama.cpp app on 2026-07-10 (PR #21), then shipped four rapid feature phases through 2026-07-12 (PRs #22-26: settings, live models.json catalog fetch + downloads, SwiftData chat history, TTS/voice input, Apple Intelligence engine + Siri). The Flutter app (and its vendored llama.cpp source used for the old ENGINE COMPATIBILITY gate at packages/maid_llm/src/llama_cpp) now lives only on branch flutter-legacy / tag v2.2.0-flutter, frozen since 2024-08-09. docs/weekly-slm-routine.md (this automation's own spec) was not updated for the pivot and still points at file paths that no longer exist on main.

CRITICAL GAP: the new native engine is NOT version-pinned. scripts/fetch-llama.sh always downloads whatever is the LATEST ggml-org/llama.cpp GitHub release at build time — no tag/commit is recorded anywhere in the repo, the resulting Frameworks/llama.xcframework is gitignored (not committed), there is no CI that would capture which version went into any given build, and no App Store release/tag exists yet for the native app (README still self-describes as 'Phase 0 — engine spike', which is itself stale given Phases 1-4 already merged). This means there is currently NO reliable, checkable source of truth for which GGUF architectures the shipping engine supports — the ENGINE COMPATIBILITY hard gate (quality bar #5) cannot be verified against a stable reference. Until fetch-llama.sh is pinned to an explicit tag/commit (recorded in-repo) or a real App Store release ships with recorded engine version, catalog-compatibility checks in this routine are working from the OLD flutter-legacy llm_arch enum as the conservative fallback, since it's the only fixed, inspectable reference and it's plausible some live installs are still running that build.

3) DEEP-DIVE: 'Same file. Same bytes. Nearly 6x the RAM.' — a byte-identical 355MB GGUF (LFM2.5-350M) costs 56-85MB RAM on Apple Silicon/visionOS vs 300-330MB on Android/Linux SBC, same inference engine (Cactus) on every device, per Cactus Compute's own 2026-03-31 benchmark post (fetched directly, not summarized secondhand, to get the author's own causal explanation verbatim: Apple's mmap() stays reclaimable file-backed memory, many Android devices' mmap() degrades to malloc()+read() due to SELinux/vendor memory management). Genuinely distinct from all three prior theses (see deepDiveThesesUsed) — this is about post-load runtime RAM, not architecture recognition, quant-label variance, or engine-version tracking. Connected honestly to privateSLM's own minRamMb heuristic (file-size x a constant, same as the rest of the industry) as an open measurement question, not a claimed fix.
